subject: Post-call recap & pilot proposal: SafeMed data handling questions
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Luca Rinaldi <luca.rinaldi@safemed-analytics.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Post-call recap & pilot proposal: SafeMed data handling questions

Hi Luca — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same playbook: 

Summary of requirements you raised:
- Strong preference for zero retention of any PII from inference payloads (customer/user identifiers, full names, national IDs).
- Short-lived session continuity for chat UX is acceptable, but must be configurable per customer and limited to non-identifiable tokens where possible.
- EU data residency for model runtime and KV/cache storage.
- Need to see SOC 2 evidence, and require a DPA with a few carve-outs around log retention for incident investigations.

Options we discussed (high-level):
1) Private (VPC) deployment: Dedicated control plane + customer-managed KMS. This lets SafeMed set retention to 0 for request/response storage and host runtime entirely in eu-central region.
2) Hosted API with tailored retention profile: Redwood hosted runtime but we apply a strict redaction pipeline for PII at ingestion, and a custom retention window (e.g., 0 days for PII, 7 days for minimal KV for session continuity).

Proposed pilot (low friction, 2 weeks):
- Ephemeral-first configuration: ingress redaction -> ephemeral KV only (7d TTL by default) -> no persistent request/response logs containing PII.
- Scoped audit logs (admin-level) retained for up to 90 days but with automated PII scrubbing before storage.
- Proof-of-concept deployment in eu-central with telemetry access for SafeMed security review.

Ask from SafeMed to proceed:
- Confirm whether you need KV disabled entirely or just configured to drop PII fields.
- Share the completed security questionnaire you mentioned (we agreed you would email it).
- Flag any specific legal language you require in the DPA (we can send a redline).

Next steps
- I'll loop in CS and Privacy engineering to validate exact feasibility and estimated timeline (target: internal reply within 24 business hours).
- If you agree to the pilot, we'll provision a short-lived tenant and share a secure link to the configuration.
- We can prepare a DocuSign DPA draft with the SafeMed requested carve-outs for your legal team to mark up.

Proposed times for an ops/architecture follow-up: Tue 10/27 10:00–11:00 CET or Wed 10/28 14:00–15:00 CET — please confirm what works.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T11:06:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pilot proposal: SafeMed data handling questions

Grace — thanks for the clean recap. Internal notes / feasibility checklist below so Luca has a fast answer once we respond: 

Feasibility summary (privacy engineering):
- 0-retention for PII: achievable via the ingest-redaction pipeline. We can redact fields deterministically (hashing or removal) before they hit any persistent store.
- KV cache concerns: by default KV is in-memory and used for short lived session state. We can provision a tenant with KV disabled OR with an enforced PII-scrub hook that removes identified PHI/PII tokens before caching. The scrub hook is slightly higher ops cost but doable for pilots.
- Audit logs: we cannot entirely remove operational metadata (trace ids, timestamps) for debugging; however we can configure redaction rules and reduce retention (e.g., 90 days) and restrict access.
- Residency: eu-central deployment is straightforward for Dedicated; hosted will require routing to eu-only pools and we need marketing-approved SLO notes for latency.

Proposed scoped exception name: SafeMed_PII_zero_7d_kv — pilots runs with KV on but scrubbed, and agree to disable KV if any PII bleed found during testing.

Action items for internal owners:
- Karthik: please prepare a short technical note on ingest redaction + KV scrub hook and any expected feature flags we must enable. (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Aditya: Legal/commercial — prepare redwood-dpa-draft.pdf with the DPA baseline and mark the sections we expect SafeMed to push back on.
- Grace: confirm desired pilot start date and whether SafeMed requires us to pre-sign the DPA before provisioning.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Luca Rinaldi <luca.rinaldi@safemed-analytics.eu>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: SafeMed Privacy <privacy@safemed-analytics.eu>
Date: 2026-10-25T11:42:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pilot proposal: SafeMed data handling questions

Thanks Grace — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our privacy/legal side: 

1) KV: we prefer KV disabled for any production user data. For a pilot we can accept a scrubbed KV if you can demonstrate that scrubbed entries are non-reversible and not linkable to user identities.
2) Audit logs: we will accept 90-day retention for operational logs but require that any request/response payloads that contain PII are not persisted beyond the ingest pipeline.
3) Residency: all processing and KV must remain within eu-central. No US replication for the pilot.

I have attached the completed security questionnaire and a first-pass DPA redline (see attached). We are ready to run a pilot next week provided you can present a configuration doc that lists the exact hooks and retention windows.

Desired pilot timeline: start Mon 10/26; 2-week pilot with a checkpoint at day 7.

Attachments: SafeMed_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (our redline)

Best,
Luca
Head of Product, SafeMed Analytics
luca.rinaldi@safemed-analytics.eu

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Luca Rinaldi <luca.rinaldi@safemed-analytics.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T14:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & pilot proposal: SafeMed data handling questions

Luca — received, and thanks for the attachments. Quick replies inline and confirmed next steps below.

> 1) KV: we prefer KV disabled for any production user data. For a pilot we can accept a scrubbed KV if you can demonstrate that scrubbed entries are non-reversible and not linkable to user identities.

Understood. Proposed approach for the pilot: enable KV for session continuity but with the following controls:
- Deterministic one-way hashing for any fields flagged as identifiers, then run a non-reversible redact pass before cache write.
- A policy that automatically drops any key that contains a configured identifier pattern (SSNs, emails).
- If SafeMed prefers, we will stand up an alternate tenant with KV disabled — that takes an extra provisioning day but we can do it before Monday if legal needs it.

> 2) Audit logs: we will accept 90-day retention for operational logs but require that any request/response payloads that contain PII are not persisted beyond the ingest pipeline.

Confirmed. We will provide a short technical doc listing the exact log buckets, retention periods, and role-based access controls.

> 3) Residency: all processing and KV must remain within eu-central. No US replication for the pilot.

Confirmed — pilot will be eu-central only. No cross-region replication.

Next steps (I will action today):
- Marissa/Karthik: please finalize the pilot config doc (include feature flags, KV scrub hook logic, and fields that are redacted).
- Aditya: send the DPA redline to Luca via DocuSign link; confirm whether Redwood needs the DPA signed pre-provisioning or accepts it signed after the pilot kickoff.
- Luca/Legal: if you can sign the DocuSign or reply with line comments by EOD Friday, we can still meet the Monday 10/26 pilot start if SafeMed is OK with the tenant being labeled "pilot — KV scrubbed".

Proposed meeting: Mon 10/26 09:30 CET — 30m to walk through config and provisioning. I'll send an invite when Luca confirms.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
